summary.intent: Remove legacy config tables and related cruft from the callisto repo (follow-on to PR #351): legacy config structs and migration code, a no-op setup_git_user action input, the installer's unsafe git `main` fallback, and update the child-process credential scrub list.
summary.outcome: Removed the two legacy config tables with their migration code, tests and docs, deleted the no-op action input, made the installer fail closed instead of falling back to git, and updated the credential scrub lists. Full CI passed and a PR for the legacy removal was committed, pushed and opened.

repo: Config handling is split between crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs (raw structs) and resolve.rs (resolution/migration logic); legacy tables touched both plus tests in callisto-cli and callisto-graph.

Credential scrubbing for child processes is defined in several places that must stay in sync: callisto-graph release provider registry.rs, callisto-cli runner.rs, and callisto-model registry.rs, with a parallel redaction list and tests (credential matrix, redaction invariant, Python build credential test).

The setup-callisto GitHub action has shell-based contract tests (e.g. tests/test_crates_io_fallback.sh) that run in CI as workflow-contract checks and assert installer behavior, so installer changes require updating them.
docs/specs/release.json and docs/config.md document config options and error specs (e.g. ERR-03) and must be updated alongside config removals.
Repo uses changesets (.changeset/*.md) for change tracking, and a single full CI command that runs format and all checks.
A 'remote origin already exists' line in CI output comes from a test fixture and is expected noise.

code.finding: Installer had an unsafe fallback to installing from git `main` when attestation/crates.io install was unavailable; it was removed so `latest` fails closed.
Test previously asserted the git-source fallback; now asserts that `latest` fails closed with no git install.

workflow: Iterating on full CI after each fix surfaced follow-on failures in order (unused constant, redaction invariant test, Python build credential test, then workflow-contract shell test); fixing tests that asserted removed behavior is a recurring step in removals.
Removing a constant or feature can leave unused items that fail lint in CI (e.g. unused E197 constant), so rerun CI after deletions.
PR body was written to a temp file and passed to the PR creation command.

friction: Multiple CI reruns needed: unused constant, redaction invariant test, Python build credential test, and the workflow-contract fallback test each failed in sequence after the changes.
Legacy references were scattered across code, tests, docs, specs and action scripts, requiring repeated grep/read passes.
